summary: Modern databases have evolved beyond storage into AI execution engines, embedding vector search, LLM inference, and ML model training directly into the query layer. By 2026, vector database adoption has grown 377% year over year, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search capabilities, pushing every major platform to integrate these features natively. The result is a landscape where teams can run RAG pipelines, embedding generation, and predictive ML without moving data out of their primary data platform.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI is a suite of fully managed AI and ML capabilities running natively inside the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. It includes Cortex LLM Functions for text summarization, classification, translation, and sentiment analysis via SQL; Cortex Analyst for natural language to SQL query generation; Cortex Search for hybrid vector and keyword retrieval; and Cortex Fine-tuning for customizing LLMs on proprietary data. As of February 2026, Snowflake Postgres runs natively in the AI Data Cloud and integrates with pgvector for vector similarity search, while Cortex provides text-to-SQL and embedding generation directly against Postgres data. All compute stays within the Snowflake security perimeter with no data egress to external model providers.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM functions via COMPLETE(), EMBED_TEXT_768(), EMBED_TEXT_1024() and others in SQL; supports Mistral, Llama 3, Snowflake Arctic, and Reka models; Cortex Analyst provides text-to-SQL; integrates with Snowflake Postgres via pgvector extension for vector similarity search
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex LLM functions are billed in Snowflake credits per token consumed; embedding functions also consume credits; Cortex Search has additional compute costs; Snowflake Postgres pricing follows standard Snowflake compute and storage credits; no separate licensing fee for Cortex features beyond credit consumption

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using standard SQL directly inside BigQuery, covering logistic regression, boosted trees, matrix factorization, time series forecasting with ARIMA+, and deep neural networks. BigQuery Vector Search adds native approximate nearest neighbor search over ARRAY<FLOAT64> embedding columns using the VECTOR_SEARCH() SQL function. Vertex AI integration enables remote model inference so BigQuery can call Gemini and other Vertex AI hosted models inline during SQL queries via ML.GENERATE_TEXT() and ML.EMBED_TEXT(), enabling RAG pipelines, summarization, and classification without data leaving Google Cloud. Embeddings can be generated at scale using ML.EMBED_TEXT against Vertex AI embedding endpoints.
databases.llm_integration: ML.GENERATE_TEXT() calls Gemini Pro, Gemini Flash, and other Vertex AI models from SQL; ML.EMBED_TEXT() generates embeddings via Vertex AI text embedding models; VECTOR_SEARCH() performs ANN search over stored embeddings; supports grounding and RAG workflows natively
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML training and inference billed per byte processed for SQL queries plus model-specific costs; VECTOR_SEARCH queries billed as standard BigQuery on-demand query pricing per TB scanned; Vertex AI model calls billed separately per 1K characters or tokens depending on model; BigQuery ML included in BigQuery pricing with no additional platform fee

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds a native vector data type and similarity search operators to Postgres, supporting exact and approximate nearest neighbor search via IVFFlat and HNSW indexing algorithms. It requires no new infrastructure, uses the same security model, backup procedures, and tooling as the existing Postgres instance, making it the lowest-friction path to vector search. pgai is a complementary extension from Timescale that adds SQL functions to call external LLM providers including OpenAI, Ollama, and Anthropic directly from Postgres queries, enabling embedding generation, text completion, and moderation checks inside SQL. For most teams, pgvector on Postgres is recommended as the best vector database for RAG in 2026, handling up to 50 million vectors effectively. Snowflake Postgres now runs natively in the AI Data Cloud with pgvector integration, and pgvector also integrates well with Databricks.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension provides pg_openai_embed(), pg_openai_complete(), and similar SQL functions calling OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and Ollama APIs; Snowflake Cortex adds text-to-SQL and embedding generation when running on Snowflake Postgres; no native built-in LLM but integrates with any external provider via pgai
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are free and open-source extensions with no licensing cost; compute costs depend on the hosting platform (self-hosted, AWS RDS, Supabase, Neon, Snowflake Postgres, etc.); external LLM API calls via pgai are billed by the respective provider; Snowflake Postgres charges standard Snowflake credits

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Redshift ML allows users to create, train, and invoke ML models using SQL CREATE MODEL statements; it automatically exports data to Amazon S3, trains models in Amazon SageMaker AutoPilot, and imports the model back as a SQL function callable in queries, supporting classification, regression, and K-means clustering. Aurora ML integrates Amazon Aurora (MySQL and PostgreSQL compatible) with SageMaker and Amazon Comprehend, enabling SQL functions that call hosted ML model endpoints for inference directly during database queries. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector as an extension for native vector similarity search, enabling RAG workloads without leaving the database. Redshift supports approximate nearest neighbor vector similarity search natively for embedding-based workloads, and integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference from SQL via the ML.PREDICT function family.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora PostgreSQL supports pgvector for vector search plus Amazon Comprehend integration for NLP; Redshift ML integrates with Amazon Bedrock via SageMaker endpoints for LLM inference in SQL; supports calling Titan, Claude, and other Bedrock models for text generation and embedding tasks from query context
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML model training billed through SageMaker AutoPilot per training hour; prediction inference billed per query in Redshift standard compute; Aurora ML charges standard Aurora instance pricing plus SageMaker endpoint costs per invocation; pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL has no additional licensing cost beyond standard Aurora pricing; Bedrock model calls billed per token by Amazon Bedrock separately

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.ai_feature: Databricks AI — MLflow, DBRX, Mosaic AI, and Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides an integrated AI platform combining MLflow for end-to-end ML lifecycle management (experiment tracking, model registry, deployment, and observability), Mosaic AI for training and fine-tuning LLMs at scale, and DBRX as Databricks' own open-source mixture-of-experts LLM. Databricks Vector Search is a native serverless vector database built into the Lakehouse that automatically syncs with Delta Lake tables, supports real-time and batch indexing, and provides ANN search via REST API and Python SDK. Databricks AI Gateway provides a unified endpoint for calling external LLMs including OpenAI, Anthropic, and self-hosted models with governance, rate limiting, and cost tracking. Mosaic AI Model Serving hosts custom and foundation models as scalable REST endpoints. pgvector integrates well with Databricks for teams using Postgres alongside the Lakehouse.
databases.llm_integration: Databricks AI Gateway provides governed access to OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, and self-hosted models from notebooks and pipelines; DBRX open-source LLM available for self-hosting or via Databricks Model Serving; Mosaic AI supports LLM fine-tuning with proprietary data; Foundation Model APIs provide pay-per-token access to Llama 3, DBRX, and Mixtral from within Databricks
databases.pricing_notes: MLflow is open-source and free; Databricks Vector Search billed in Databricks Units (DBUs) per hour of serverless compute; Foundation Model API billed per token consumed; Model Serving billed per DBU per hour of endpoint uptime plus per-request costs; Mosaic AI training billed by GPU compute hours; overall cost rolls into Databricks platform subscription or pay-as-you-go DBU pricing

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is a native capability of MongoDB Atlas that stores vector embeddings directly alongside operational document data in the same collection, enabling semantic similarity search without a separate vector store. It uses an HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) index for approximate nearest neighbor search and is queried via the MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline using the $vectorSearch stage, allowing vector search to be combined with standard MongoDB filters, projections, and joins in a single query. Atlas Vector Search integrates with major embedding providers including OpenAI, Cohere, and HuggingFace, and is a first-class component in LangChain, LlamaIndex, and other RAG frameworks. Atlas also offers Atlas Stream Processing and Atlas SQL Interface, enabling hybrid transactional, analytical, and AI workloads on one platform without ETL. As of 2026, MongoDB Atlas is listed among the top enterprise vector databases with strong adoption in production RAG applications.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates natively with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Hugging Face as a vector store backend; supports OpenAI, Cohere, and Voyage AI embedding models for automatic embedding generation via Atlas triggers or application layer; Atlas integrations marketplace provides pre-built connectors to OpenAI and Azure OpenAI for end-to-end RAG pipeline setup
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is included in Atlas clusters with no separate feature cost; billed through standard Atlas cluster pricing based on cluster tier (M10 and above support Vector Search); dedicated search nodes for vector workloads available at additional cost per node hour; free tier (M0) does not support Vector Search indexes; costs scale with cluster size, storage, and data transfer
